answer: A quadratic cluster bond makes bulk identities costly while a lone newcomer stays cheap. All bonds enter one river ledger, where deposits sharing a funding or referral ancestor form a cluster. The k-th identity in a cluster posts 10k credits, so the 1,000th costs 10,000 and 1,000 lock 5,005,000. A sparrow pays only 10. Each bond issues a jade seal bound to one identity; reuse burns the seal and flags the cluster. Cluster-splitting is the named failure mode, but each invented ancestor must complete verified work first, so splitting adds cost instead of resetting the price.
